name: A real healthy whole blood (GSM7508429)
about: Every site of IAM-Atlas v2.1 has one fixed place on this globe, the same as on the atlas's cell pages. Drag to turn it. The healthy reference is healthy blood for this person's own cell mix (IAM-Atlas v2.1, Stage D21 shares), compared at 773,556 sites. The change is fixed by the measurement: a site has changed when it lies outside the healthy range. The slider only fades the healthy background, so you can see the change by itself. A picture: nothing is scored from it; Met-A and the C-Score read against their own commissioned reference, which is also a layer. The atlas blends 21 sources and sits slightly closer to 0.5 than one array, so a healthy sample shows a faint even difference. In a woman one X chromosome is held methylated, so her X shows as a patch against a reference that pools both sexes. A small loss spread over many sites shows on the departures layer, not the whole genome.

layers.note: Against healthy blood for this person's own cell mix (IAM-Atlas v2.1, Stage D21 shares). Each site's difference is measured in that site's healthy width (how much healthy people vary there, and how sure the atlas is), in this sample's own spread; a site has changed beyond 3, the C-Score's rule. The line is set by the measurement, not by the reader. Red: more methylation than healthy; blue: less; brighter: further out.
